documents.title: ResearchTeam
documents.snippet: Conduct rigorous, source-grounded scholarly research with agent-based workflows and robust update safety.
paragraphs: Conduct rigorous, source-grounded scholarly research with agent-based workflows and robust update safety.

ResearchTeam is a pip-installable framework for producing well-structured research reports with verified citations, using agent-based workflows. All claims are grounded in peer-reviewed or reputable scholarly sources, with Chicago-style citations. Once installed, a derived project can receive infrastructure updates automatically — without touching user research content.
```bash pip install git+https://github.com/jlcatonjr/researchteam.git ```
`init` scaffolds a complete project directory, runs `git init`, and makes an initial commit. Edit `brief.json` to describe your project before running any agents.
```bash git clone https://github.com/jlcatonjr/researchteam.git my-research-project cd my-research-project ```
Then follow the onboarding steps in `CLAUDE.md` or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
- `name` — directory to create (defaults to current directory if empty) - `--ref` — upstream git ref to scaffold from (default: `main`) - `--remote` — git remote URL to set as `origin` after init

- `--yes / -y` — skip interactive confirmation; required in CI - `--dry-run` — show what would change without writing files - `--layer2-only` — only sync layer-2 files; skip `agentteams --update --merge` - `--ref` — override the upstream ref (default: value in `.researchteam` marker)
ResearchTeam infrastructure is split into two independently updatable layers:
**User-owned files** (`brief.json`, `Projects/`, `references/`) are never touched by either update layer.
`researchteam update` (without `--layer2-only`) runs both layers in sequence.
Projects created with `researchteam init` receive a `.github/workflows/agentteams-sync.yml` that runs both layers automatically on a weekly schedule and on `workflow_dispatch`. The CI:

1. Installs the `researchteam` CLI and runs `researchteam update --layer2-only --yes` 2. Installs the `agentteams` CLI and runs `agentteams --update --merge --yes` 3. Validates changed paths and fence integrity 4. Optionally opens a PR with the combined diff (manual runs with `open_pr=true`)

The orchestrator agent is the entry point for all agent-based workflows. It coordinates requests, enforces constitutional rules, and ensures every multi-file session closes with a consistency check. **Do not bypass the orchestrator or invoke agents directly, except for the Team Builder bootstrap flow.**

- **Orchestrator:** Coordinates all agent operations and workflow routing. - **Domain Agents:** Specialized for research, writing, validation, reference management, and more. See `.github/copilot-instructions.md` for the full agent team list and roles. - **Note on topology:** `.github/agents/references/pipeline-graph.md` is auto-generated from `build_team.py`. Fenced regions are blocks managed by agents. **Do not edit inside fenced regions manually.** User-authored content outside these regions is preserved during updates.

documents.title: Domain Boundary — Memory-Index Vector vs Retrieval-Integrator
documents.snippet: The agentteams `memory_index` module ships a `--query-strategy vector` mode that is a **local sparse tf-idf vector-space ranking for memory-history retrieval only**. It is stdlib-only, deterministic, and scoped to durable text sources (work
paragraphs: The agentteams `memory_index` module ships a `--query-strategy vector` mode that is a **local sparse tf-idf vector-space ranking for memory-history retrieval only**. It is stdlib-only, deterministic, and scoped to durable text sources (work summaries, CHANGELOG, durable plans).

It is **separate** from any project-level retrieval-integrator validation contract (e.g., relational metadata retrieval against project data tables). When a project's retrieval contract has `mode: relational-metadata`, that is independent from the memory-index's `vector_runtime_mode: sparse-tfidf-cosine` — the two retrieval surfaces address different questions and must not be conflated.

documents.title: Bridge Entrypoint: copilot-vscode -> claude
documents.snippet: This is a lightweight interface bridge. Canonical agent definitions remain in source framework files. Use orchestrator-first routing for team-based work.
paragraphs: This is a lightweight interface bridge. Canonical agent definitions remain in source framework files. Use orchestrator-first routing for team-based work.
Before falling back to grep / filesystem search for thematic or cross-summary questions, query the agentteams memory-index:
``` agentteams --query-index "<the user's question>" --query-strategy vector --query-k 5 ```

Some installations require `--description PATH` for read-only queries — pass the project brief if so. The index covers durable prose (work summaries, plans, CHANGELOG, references), NOT code. For code-symbol lookups, grep remains primary.

See `domain-boundary.md` (this directory) for the boundary between the memory-index vector mode and project-level retrieval-integrator validation contracts — they address different questions and must not be conflated.

paragraphs: **Plan name:** egyptian-cosmopolitanism **Trigger:** User request — April 18, 2026 **Goal:** Produce a scholarly research report examining Egyptian cosmopolitan life before mass Jewish emigration (pre-1948), the impact on religious tolerance, and transformation over the following half-century, with attention to Coptic and Eastern Orthodox communities. **Output directory:** `EgyptianDevelopment/`

1. `@topic-scoping-expert` → Research plan and source strategy 2. `@literature-review-expert` → Survey of scholarly literature 3. `@main-analysis-expert` → Core analysis 4. `@conclusion-expert` → Conclusion and executive summary 5. `@reference-manager` → Compile and verify bibliography.bib

- Minimum 12 Chicago Author-Date citations, all verifiable via DOI or repository record - Covers: pre-1948 cosmopolitan Egypt; Jewish emigration and its causes; impact on religious pluralism; Coptic community treatment; Eastern Orthodox (Greek, Armenian) communities; transformation 1948–2000 - No fabricated references - Full Chicago bibliography appended
All outputs in `EgyptianDevelopment/` — remove folder to revert.
